verdict.rationale: Typesense advertises itself as a 'typo-tolerant search engine' out of the box and ships a dedicated 'Tuning Typo Tolerance' guide for controlling fuzzy-match behavior, corroborated by community praise for 'fuzzy text matching' and 'handling typographic errors out-of-the-box'. A hands-on probe confirms a real roundtrip: indexing a doc and querying with a misspelling ('serch infra') returned correct highlighted results, validating the built-in typo tolerance claim. Missing for 10: explicit documentation excerpt of the specific tunable parameters (e.g. num_typos, min word length thresholds) rather than just the page title reference.
